title: PUMA Philippine Half Marathon Manila Leg 2026 Review: What the 2025 Race Was Like
seo_title: PUMA Manila Half Marathon Review: 3am Start, Humidity, Cut-offs
meta_description: PUMA Manila Half Marathon review: the 2025 race at SM Mall of Asia, a 3am start in 25°C saturated air, a four-hour cut-off, drinks every 2-2.5 km, finisher items and how fast the field ran.
dek: What running the Manila leg of the PUMA Philippine Half Series was like in 2025: the 3am start, the humidity, the cut-offs and sweep, the aid and finisher items, and how fast you need to be to place.
verdict: Enter if you want a big Metro Manila half marathon with a forgiving cut-off and a six-city series medal to chase. The 2025 race put 2,371 runners through the 21 km, with four hours to finish, drinks about every 2 to 2.5 km, and a medal, towel and shirt for finishers. The front is not fast: the winners ran 1:23 and 1:31, and half the field took longer than 2:47. The catch is the hour and the air. The half started at 3am, when Manila's airport recorded 25°C, a 25°C dew point, 100% humidity and no wind. Pace for the humidity, and check the 2026 route when it is published, because none was posted on the race pages in 2025.

sections.heading: Start Times and Cut-offs: A 3am Half With Four Hours to Finish
paragraphs: The half marathon started at 3am, the 10 km at 4.30am and the 5 km at 5am, all from the SM Mall of Asia Concert Grounds in Pasay [1][2]. The cut-offs were four hours for the half, two hours for the 10 km and one hour for the 5 km [1]. Runners had to cross the start within 15 minutes of their flag-off or be disqualified [1].

From 7am an ambulance swept the course, picking up anyone still out and taking them to the finish, and the organiser said those runners would be disqualified from the official results [2]. The published results do list 24 half marathoners with gun times over four hours, the slowest 4:20:41 [3], but a runner aiming at four hours should not count on being one of them.

sections.heading: The Weather: Saturated Air Before Dawn
paragraphs: Ninoy Aquino International Airport, about 5 km south-east of the start, recorded 25°C at 3am on race morning, with a dew point of 25°C, 100% humidity and a 1-knot wind [4]. Nothing changed until 6am. It was 27°C with 94% humidity at 7am, when the sweep began, 29°C at 8am and 31°C at 9am [4].

When the dew point equals the air temperature, sweat barely evaporates, so the body loses its main way of cooling and heart rate climbs at a pace that would feel easy in drier air. Almost the whole half-marathon field finished inside four hours, before 7am [3], so most runners never met the heat of the day, only the wet air. Start slower than your usual half-marathon pace and use every drinks station.
Christine Hallasgo, who won the women's 10 km, said each city in the series brings different routes and climates, and that runners who do not know an area take time to adjust [5].

sections.heading: The Course: No Map on the Race Pages
paragraphs: The organiser billed the race as a celebration of Metro Manila's landmarks and heritage [6]. Its race rules said the route map would be announced later, and the race's registration pages still carry no map [1][6]. Sections of the route were closed to traffic, walkers were asked to keep to the right so faster runners could pass, and bikes, skates, strollers and wheelchairs were not allowed on the course [2].

sections.heading: Aid Stations and Finisher Items
paragraphs: Drinks stations were placed roughly every 2 to 2.5 km, with water and sports drink, and bananas for the longer distances; Gatorade was the official sports drink [1][7]. Medical staff were on the course and at the start and finish, and the venue had baggage tents for each distance, changing areas and portable toilets [1][2].

Every entry included a PUMA race singlet and a bib with a timing chip [1][6]. Finishers of all three distances got a medal, a towel and a loot bag; only 21 km finishers got the PUMA finisher's shirt, and the 21 km medal has its own design [6]. Only runners who completed the distance they registered for received the finisher items [1].

sections.heading: How Fast the Field Is
paragraphs: The results list 2,371 runners in the 21 km, 2,764 in the 10 km and 2,264 in the 5 km [3]. In the half, 1,629 men and 736 women were ranked [3].

Simon Enriquez, described as a newcomer, won the men's half in 1:23:05, from Joram Lava in 1:24:23 and Moiselle Angelo Alforque in 1:25:22. Maricar Camacho won the women's race in 1:30:54, ahead of Jennelyn Isibido in 1:37:11 [7]. Tenth place was 1:37:51 for men and 2:03:34 for women, so a woman under 2:03 would have made the top ten [3].

That is a soft front for a half marathon: at the 2026 Clark leg of the same series, the winners ran 1:09:23 and 1:21:00 [8]. The middle of the field is relaxed too. The median finish was 2:47:39, 178 runners broke two hours and 1,566 of the 2,361 ranked finishers broke three [3].

The 10 km was won by Rico Jay Patanao in 32:44 and by Christine Hallasgo, the 2019 SEA Games marathon gold medallist, in 38:32 [7][5]. Tenth place in the 10 km was 47:38 for men and 58:05 for women [3].

sections.heading: Race Weekend Logistics
paragraphs: There was no race-day registration, but runners who missed kit collection could pick up their kits at the venue on race morning, and swap a singlet for another size there if stock allowed [2]. Entry in 2025 cost ₱2,200 for the 21 km, ₱1,600 for the 10 km and ₱1,400 for the 5 km, plus processing and web fees [1]. The 21 km sold out in every city of the series [5].

Entries cannot be refunded, transferred or deferred, and you cannot change distance or city leg after registering [1][2]. You may withdraw, but without a refund, and only typing errors, contact details and addresses can be corrected, at the on-site registration area [2]. The minimum age is 18 for the 21 km, 16 for the 10 km and 13 for the 5 km [1]. The organiser pointed runners to taxis, Grab, buses and other public transport, and listed parking as to be announced [2].

Awards were presented at the venue straight after the race, and winners had to be there to collect them [1][2]. Results were promised within one to two days, and a protest had to be lodged in writing within an hour of results going up, with a non-refundable ₱5,000 fee [1]. Runners who complete all six legs of the series get an extra All-City Legacy Medal [5].

sections.heading: Should You Enter the 2026 Race?
paragraphs: Yes, if you want a big, well-supplied half marathon in Metro Manila with a forgiving four-hour cut-off, or you are collecting the series' six-city medal. It suits first-time half marathoners, since half the 2025 field took longer than 2:47 [3], and it gives a good club runner a real chance of a top-ten place.
Think twice if you want a cool morning for a personal best, if you cannot face a 3am start, or if you want to study the route before you enter.

The 2026 Manila leg is on Sunday 11 October at the MOA Concert Grounds, the last race of the 2026 series, after Clark in August and Cagayan de Oro on 6 September [8][9]. Fees rise to ₱2,300, ₱1,700 and ₱1,500, and the cut-offs stay at four hours, two hours and one hour [10]. The registration page lists a 3am start, but the gun time for each distance and the route had not been published when this was written [10][9].
Nobody from this site ran the race. This review draws on the organiser's race rules, FAQ and race information, the full results, airport weather records and Philippine news reports.

faqs.question: What time does the PUMA Manila Half Marathon start?
faqs.answer: Very early. In 2025 the 21 km started at 3am, the 10 km at 4.30am and the 5 km at 5am, from the SM Mall of Asia Concert Grounds, and runners had to start within 15 minutes of their flag-off. For 11 October 2026 the registration page lists a 3am start; gun times per distance were still to be announced.

faqs.question: What are the cut-off times at the PUMA Manila Half Marathon?
faqs.answer: Four hours for the 21 km, two hours for the 10 km and one hour for the 5 km, in 2025 and again for 2026. In 2025 an ambulance swept the course from 7am and took any remaining runners to the finish, and the organiser said they would be disqualified from the official results.

faqs.question: How humid is the PUMA Manila Half Marathon?
faqs.answer: Very. At the 3am start in 2025, Manila's airport recorded 25°C, a dew point of 25°C, 100% humidity and almost no wind, and it stayed that way until 6am. It reached 27°C by 7am and 31°C by 9am. Sweat barely evaporates in air like that, so start slower than your usual pace.

faqs.question: How fast do you need to be to place at the PUMA Manila Half Marathon?
faqs.answer: Not very fast by half-marathon standards. In 2025 the winners ran 1:23:05 and 1:30:54, and tenth place was 1:37:51 for men and 2:03:34 for women. The median finish was 2:47:39. By comparison, the 2026 Clark leg of the same series was won in 1:09:23 and 1:21:00.

faqs.question: What do finishers get at the PUMA Manila Half Marathon?
faqs.answer: In 2025 every finisher got a medal, a towel and a loot bag, on top of the PUMA race singlet and bib in the race kit. Only 21 km finishers received the PUMA finisher's shirt. Runners who complete all six legs of the PUMA Philippine Half Series also earn an All-City Legacy Medal.

faqs.question: Can you transfer or refund a PUMA Manila Half Marathon entry?
faqs.answer: No. Entries cannot be refunded, transferred or deferred, and you cannot switch distance or city leg after registering. You may withdraw, but you will not get your money back. Only typing errors, contact details and addresses can be corrected, at the on-site registration area.

editorial_notes: Rewritten 2026-09-28 about the previous Manila race (Sunday 5 October 2025). Weather is from airport METAR observations, not a forecast. Field sizes, placings, the median and the sub-two and sub-three counts are computed from the full Race Roster results. No 2025 route map could be found on the race pages, and the organiser's social media posts need a login, so the course is not described. The results list a pacer third among women; the podium given is the one Philstar and the awards list report. Ten 21 km results marked 'Quarantine' with no place are left out. No rating.
